findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket (including the seeded vendor-roster.xlsx) are not encrypted at rest by default.

findings.issue_category: missing access control / no ACL specified
findings.description: No 'acl' attribute is set, so the bucket relies on AWS default (private) but without explicit private ACL or public-access-block configuration there is no defense-in-depth against accidental public exposure, especially combined with force_destroy and no encryption.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving ledger export data unencrypted at rest despite likely containing sensitive financial data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, leaving operational runbook content (which may include sensitive operational procedures or credentials references) unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL; it appears to be a typo of 'log-delivery-write' or similar, which could either break logging entirely or unintentionally apply a broader/log-delivery style ACL, weakening access control on the audit trail bucket that holds sensitive audit/log data.

force_destroy = true is set on a bucket without versioning or encryption, allowing all objects to be permanently deleted along with the bucket, increasing the risk of irreversible data loss if the bucket is removed maliciously or accidentally.
